question: What national default school-zone speed limit must every jurisdiction post, regardless of local law or engineering study?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence does not support the premise of the question — the MUTCD does not establish any national default school-zone speed limit value that every jurisdiction must post. Instead, reduced school speed limit zones are established either on the basis of an engineering study or by statute, and signing requirements attach only where such a zone has actually been established. Standards (mandatory): - "Speed zones (other than statutory speed limits) shall only be established on the basis of an engineering study that has been performed in accordance with traffic engineering practices. The engineering study shall consider the roadway context." - "A School Speed Limit assembly (see Figure 7B-1) or a School Speed Limit When Flashing (S5-1) sign (see Figure 7B-1) shall be used to indicate the speed limit where a reduced school speed limit zone has been established based upon an engineering study or where a reduced school speed limit is specified for such areas by statute." - "If a reduced school speed limit zone has been established, a School (S1-1) sign shall be installed in advance (see Table 2C-3 for advance placement guidelines) of the first School Speed Limit sign assembly or S5-1 sign that is encountered in each direction as traffic approaches the reduced school speed limit zone." Citations: - Section 2B.21 Standard §6 (p.84) - Section 7B.05 Standard §1 (p.978) - Section 7B.05 Standard §2 (p.978)
